title: Buried where he died
hookLine: he dies in Aisha's room and is buried there, now beneath the green dome in Medina

cards: A curtain hangs where a door would be. Outside it, the companions have lined up for the dawn prayer, with Abu Bakr leading. Then, Anas reports in Bukhari, the curtain lifts.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, looks out at the rows praying, and smiles. The people nearly break their lines for joy. He signals to them to finish, and lets the curtain fall.
It is one of the last things they see of him. The room behind it is Aisha's. Today, what happens in it, and why it is still there.

teach.b: Aisha tells the next part herself. In her account in Bukhari, he died in her house, on the day that was hers, with his head resting against her.

Her brother came in with a fresh tooth-stick, and she saw the Prophet's eyes follow it, so she softened it for him and he used it. Then the question of where to bury him. The companions did not agree.

teach.h: A PROPHET IS BURIED WHERE HE DIES.
teach.b: Abu Bakr settled it, according to a report in Tirmidhi, by remembering something he had heard the Prophet say: a prophet is buried in the place where he dies. They dug in the floor of the room, where the bed had been.

teach.h: A ROOM UNDER A GREEN DOME.
teach.b: Over time the mosque grew around it, and today it sits inside the Prophet's Mosque, under a green dome. Visitors stand before it and greet him: peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. That greeting points to a verse.

Surah al-Ahzab, verse fifty-six, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation." This is salawat.
Muslims say a short blessing after his name: salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam, God bless him and grant him peace. It's the little mark you see written after his name.
Here the whole sirah we have walked since this block began comes to rest: Sumayyah, the boycott, Ta'if, the cave, Quba, the treaty, Mecca's open doors, the farewell at Arafah.
Tomorrow the story turns to the people he left.

how: Muslims add a blessing of peace (salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam) whenever the Prophet is named, and visitors to the Prophet's Mosque in Medina stand before his resting place and greet him with peace.

games.q: you're among the companions. the Prophet has died in Aisha's room, and people disagree about where to bury him. what do you do?
o: carry him to the graveyard with the others.
carry him back to Mecca, where he was born.

games.why: Abu Bakr remembered him saying that a prophet is buried where he dies, so they dug in the floor of the room.

practice: Picture the small room: the curtain, the tooth-stick, the rows praying outside. If you pray, say the salawat Muslims use, salla Allahu alayhi wa sallam, quietly, a few times, at the pace of your breath.
If you don't, stay with the word peace, and send it to everyone who carried this story to you.

wordCard.voice: Salawat, the blessing Muslims add after the Prophet's name, said at the room beside the mosque where, by a saying Abu Bakr remembered, he was buried where he died. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: God bless him and grant him peace, said after the Prophet's name.

carryVoice: Your line: peace upon him. A small blessing that travels farther than any room. Day seven hundred ninety-seven, done.
